items.definition:
excessive indulgence in sensual pleasures
The novel depicted a life of wild debauchery and excess.

the introduction of a democratic system or democratic principles
The country underwent a rapid democratization process after the revolution.

energy, style, and enthusiasm
She performed the dance with great elan and grace.

a sudden blocking of an artery
The patient suffered a pulmonary embolism.

a person who supports globalism
The debate often pits nationalists against globalists.

excessive sensitivity
She suffers from hypersensitivity to certain food additives.

the introduction of semen into the female reproductive tract
Artificial insemination is a common practice in livestock breeding.

a make of car, as distinct from a specific model
Rolls-Royce is a luxury car marque.

A curved surface of a liquid; a piece of cartilage in the knee.
The doctor examined the tear in his knee's meniscus.

Something that is monstrous, especially in size or appearance.
The new building was an architectural monstrosity.

A person who exploits circumstances to gain immediate advantage.
He was criticized for being an opportunist, always looking out for himself.

An opening, especially one in the body.
The small orifice allowed water to drain slowly.

The body of peers; the rank or dignity of a peer.
He inherited the peerage after his father's death.

a story told about a past event remembered by the narrator
The old friends shared many reminiscences about their college days.

a dishonest or unscrupulous person; a rogue
The scoundrel tried to cheat the old woman out of her money.

a temporary stay
Our sojourn in the mountains was peaceful and refreshing.

a group of wild boars; a device that makes sound
A sounder of wild pigs emerged from the forest.

a person or thing that collects things or part of things together.
News aggregators collect articles from various sources.

name or title
The appellation 'Iron Lady' was given to Margaret Thatcher.

exile or expulsion
The king ordered the banishment of the traitor.

an original idea or invention
The new software was the brainchild of a young programmer.

physical strength
He relied on his brawn rather than his intellect.

responsibility for a fault or wrong
The investigation determined his culpability in the accident.

the ending of racial segregation
The desegregation of schools was a major civil rights achievement.

the act of forcing something out
The manufacturing process involves the extrusion of plastic.

a heavy revolving wheel in a machine
The engine's flywheel helps to smooth out power delivery.

the point on which a lever rests or is supported
The seesaw balanced perfectly on its fulcrum.

Surgical removal of the uterus
She underwent a hysterectomy for medical reasons.

The quality of being immediate
The immediacy of the danger was clear to everyone.

Breeding of closely related individuals
Inbreeding can lead to a reduction in genetic diversity.

The state of being in debt
The country's indebtedness grew significantly last year.

ordinary people, not clergy
The sermon was aimed at educating the laity about church doctrine.

a type of cancer of the blood
She was diagnosed with leukaemia at a young age.

the granting of a license
Obtaining licensure is a crucial step for medical professionals.

a person who inspires or influences others, especially one prominent in a particular sphere
He was considered a luminary in the field of astrophysics.

a mythical creature with the head of a bull and the body of a man
The hero Theseus famously defeated the Minotaur in the labyrinth.

a slimy substance secreted by mucous membranes
The body produces mucous to protect the lining of the respiratory tract.

subatomic particles with no electric charge
Neutrinos are notoriously difficult to detect due to their weak interaction with matter.

a common form of arthritis
Osteoarthritis often affects the knees and hips.

an outcast
After the scandal, he became a pariah in the community.

the quality or condition of being an individual person
The debate centered on the legal definition of personhood.

a direct vote of all the members of an electorate on an important public question
The government decided to hold a plebiscite on the proposed constitutional changes.

a synthetic resin used in foams, coatings, and adhesives
The furniture was upholstered in durable polyurethane fabric.

a person who is guided and supported by an older and more experienced person
The young artist was a protégé of the famous sculptor.

something done or made quickly
Let's just do a quickie review before the meeting.

a large number of ordinary people or things; a confused mass
He fought his way through the ruck of reporters.

a ring of muscle surrounding and serving to guard or close an opening or tube
The esophageal sphincter prevents stomach acid from flowing back up.

the breastbone
The ribs are connected to the sternum.

the action or process of strangling or being strangled
The cause of death was determined to be strangulation.

the arrangement or classification of something into different groups
Social stratification is a key concept in sociology.

a compound which is the chief component of cane or beet sugar
Sucrose is a disaccharide made of glucose and fructose.

news or information
She brought a tiding of joy.

protection of or authority over someone or something; guardianship
Under the tutelage of her mentor, she quickly improved.

an infectious disease caused by rickettsiae
Historically, typhus outbreaks were common during wartime.

a person without a settled home or regular work who wanders from place to place
The police picked up a vagrant sleeping on a park bench.

one who accepts; a recipient
In chemistry, an electron acceptor gains electrons.

an uncivilized or primitive state; a cruel or brutal act
The act of torture is a true barbarism.

a place where soldiers are lodged
The soldiers were assigned a billet in the village.

a dividing wall or barrier, especially in a ship or aircraft
The crew checked the integrity of the bulkhead.

the husks of corn or other seed-bearing plants
They separated the wheat from the chaff.

the green pigment in plants
Chlorophyll is essential for photosynthesis in plants.

a covered walk, especially in a monastery or cathedral
The monks walked silently through the cloister.

the belief that the universe and living organisms originate from divine creation
Creationism is a belief system that contrasts with the theory of evolution.

the doctrine that all events, including human action, are ultimately determined by causes external to the will
The debate between free will and determinism is ancient.
